clue.text: Trying individual meaning to come between scholar and class

indicators.note: tells you the word for meaning sits in the middle, flanked by the scholar and the class

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate scholar
the gist of something is its essential meaning
to rate something is to class or rank it

explanation.surface: A person who is hard work intends to get in the way of a pupil and the lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' pretends to mean tiresome; here it describes someone who hears cases in court. 'to come between' only fixes the order of the three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a justice of the peace is a person who tries cases in court.

clue.text: A word of thanks taking in a female divinity

indicators.note: the word of thanks takes in, that is swallows, the female

parts.note: ta is an informal British thank-you
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A thank-you offered while welcoming a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' is the container signal. The thank-you is the casual British one, and the 'a' before 'female' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: she is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war.

clue.text: Currently popular case for doing nothing

parts.note: what is in is fashionable at the moment
an action is a lawsuit, a case in court

explanation.surface: The fashionable argument these days is in favour of idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun phrase: idleness, the state of not acting.

clue.text: High-rise homes built by workers for their own occupation

definitions.text: High-rise homes built by workers for their own occupation

parts.words: High-rise homes built by workers for their own occupation
parts.note: the workers are insects of a white-ant colony, and their tall homes are the mounds they raise and live in

explanation.surface: Tower blocks put up by builders who then move in themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: these are the tall mounds that colonies of white ants construct and inhabit.

clue.text: Store where you find a club and other weapons

definitions.text: Store where you find a club and other weapons

parts.words: Store where you find a club and other weapons
parts.note: a club is a cudgel kept in a weapons store, and also a hint at a famous London football club of the same name

explanation.surface: A shop that sells cudgels alongside other arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'club' is doing double duty as a wink: a famous north London football club shares its name with a weapons store.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a depot for arms, and also the name of a London football team.

clue.text: A flier of sound merit

indicators.note: says the word for merit is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: to merit something is to earn it

explanation.surface: A pilot of solid worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of sound' is the homophone signal: EARN, said, gives the sea eagle beloved of crossword setters. 'sound' pretends to mean reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a sea eagle, a bird and so something that flies.

clue.text: Puts the squeeze on groups of spectators about to go off

indicators.note: the word for the crowds goes about, that is around, the word for going bad

parts.note: gates are the crowds paying to attend sports matches
food that goes off will rot

explanation.surface: Pressure is applied to crowds of onlookers who are on the point of leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 'go off' pretends to mean depart but means decay, and the spectators are the paying crowds at sports matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimly literal synonym: it strangles with a tightened cord or wire.

clue.text: Adept but unpolished equestrian?

parts.note: someone skilled enough to break in untrained horses, whose name read in two parts suggests an uncouth person on horseback

explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a horse-breaker is highly skilled, though the name suggests someone coarse in the saddle.

clue.text: Chafe at nothing with rhythmic variety

parts.note: to chafe is to rub
taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Getting irritated over trifles, in a changeable tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical direction: played with flexible tempo, speeding and slowing for expression.

clue.text: Places of entertainment causing the shedding of tears

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shedding suggests the letters being scattered about and falling in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Venues for shows that make the audience weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shedding of' is the anagram signal and acts only on the last word, giving ATRES; 'causing' joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: playhouses are venues where people go to be entertained.

clue.text: Service flat — bargain price!

parts.note: a flat surface is an even one
something bought for a song is bought very cheaply

explanation.surface: A serviced apartment going cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service flat' reads as one thing but splits: the service is a church one. 'For a song' is the idiom for a bargain price.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the Anglican evening prayer, a church act of worship.

clue.text: A painter being laid off

indicators.note: off means not right, so the letters before it are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A decorator losing his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid off' reads as made redundant, but 'off' is the anagram signal acting on LAID; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Salvador, the Spanish surrealist artist.

clue.text: Remove the top and walk back with it in time

indicators.note: the turned walk and the it go inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: back tells you the word for walk is written the other way round

parts.note: to pace is to walk
taken as written

explanation.surface: Take the lid off and stroll home carrying it without being late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives ECAP, and 'in' then sets that and the next piece inside the word for time. The definition is grimmer than the innocent lid-removal suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical synonym: to behead is to take the head off.

clue.text: The negotiator will find the answer lies in farm-machinery

indicators.note: the short form of answer lies inside the farm vehicle

parts.note: a tractor is a piece of farm machinery

explanation.surface: A dealmaker will discover that agricultural equipment is the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lies in' is the container signal; 'will find the' is linking matter. The surface suggests a deal about equipment, hiding that 'answer' is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who conducts business dealings to a conclusion.

clue.text: Note trains can be thunderous

indicators.note: says these letters can be made into something else

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Observe how loud railway engines are.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: extremely loud, like the herald Stentor of the Iliad.

clue.text: Church has an attempt to obtain an endowment for singers

parts.note: taken as written
to try is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: A parish makes a bid to get funding for its choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'to obtain' are links. The singers are priests paid to chant masses for the founder's soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: a fund left to pay priests to sing masses for the donor.

clue.text: Not the accommodation for down-to earth travellers!

definitions.text: Not the accommodation for down-to earth travellers!

parts.words: Not the accommodation for down-to earth travellers!
parts.note: room for those who travel by flying, hence not for anyone who stays on the ground

explanation.surface: Lodgings that would not suit sensible, practical tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: the sky above a country, where aircraft and not ground-bound people travel.

clue.text: Relaxed model in colourful environment

indicators.note: the colourful word forms the surroundings of the other piece

parts.note: red is a colour, so something red is colourful
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: A sitter at ease in a vivid setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' makes RED the surroundings of POSE; 'in' joins the two. 'Relaxed' is a past-tense verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a past-tense verb: rested, lay at ease.

clue.text: Extra players — not very bright

parts.note: something over is left over, extra
the cast are the actors, the players, in a show

explanation.surface: Spare members of the team who are a bit dim.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather sense: a cloudy, dull sky.

clue.text: Act for pre-arranged figure

indicators.note: arranged tells you to put the three letters before the hyphen in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a figure is a shape or form

explanation.surface: Stand in for a sum agreed in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated word must be split: 'arranged' is the anagram signal acting on the three letters before the hyphen. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to play a part on stage.

clue.text: Meal in part cooked as required by convention

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are turned into something new

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Dinner partly prepared in the customary manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' is the anagram signal for MEAL IN PART; 'as required by' links to the definition, which is an assembly, not a custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a formal assembly of representatives, a legislature.

clue.text: Always included among, the Vertebrata

indicators.note: says the letters sit unbroken inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Forever classed with the animals that have backbones.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: at all times, eternally.

clue.text: Copper involved in French art work that makes money

indicators.note: the copper is wrapped up inside the other two pieces

parts.note: art is the old form of are, as in thou art; the French for that is tu es
to do is to work or perform
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Bronze used in a Parisian sculpture that turns a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French art' is not painting but the old verb in 'thou art', translated into French. 'involved in' is the container signal; 'that makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the former currency of Portugal.

clue.text: Reward the personnel officer

parts.note: to tip someone is to reward them with a gratuity
the staff are the employees of an organisation

explanation.surface: Give a bonus to the head of human resources.
explanation.walkthrough: 'personnel officer' looks like one job title, but splits: only 'officer' is the definition, an official of an English court.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a court official, originally a constable carrying a metal-capped stick.

clue.text: Care must be exercised in shaping a tree

indicators.note: exercising and shaping both say the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Pruning needs a careful hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the maple genus.

clue.text: "Sweet Flora", the golden horse one backs with some hesitation

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: backs tells you the horse and the one are written together from right to left

parts.note: a nag is a horse
I is the Roman numeral one
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A punter nervously puts money on a palomino called Sweet Flora.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' gives IGAN from the horse and the one together. 'Sweet Flora' is a fragrant plant, not a racehorse's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: the marjoram genus, aromatic herbs, so fragrant plant life.

clue.text: Get hold of the necessary equipment

definitions.meaning: to seize or grapple with someone, as in rugby
gear or kit for a task, such as fishing

explanation.surface: Obtain the kit you need.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense, to seize or grapple; noun sense, gear for a job such as angling.

clue.text: Pondering the downfall that overwhelmed the maiden.

indicators.note: what overwhelms something engulfs it, so the downfall word swallows the maiden

parts.note: ruination is a downfall or destruction
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Brooding on the disgrace that engulfed a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that overwhelmed' puts M inside RUINATION. M for maiden comes from cricket, where a maiden is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: deep thought, chewing something over.
